Checked:

  • Add Predefined Choices → 8 lists (Months, Days, Yes/No, Salutations, Priorities, Industries, Lead sources, Ratings); Months adds 12, repeat skips 12 [PASS]
  • Ready-made Source and Industry sets → System sets Source (16) and Industry (16); a pick list links to Source, values checked [PASS]
  • Which value is used where → "Where is this value used" per value: records, views, rules, blueprints, maps (works for used values; crashes for unused ones, see 2) [PASS]

Still failing:

  • Delete an unused value for good: expected One at a time from Unused; in-use refused; actual API PASS (used 422, unused 200, on records 409, two at once 422). Screen: the delete icon and "Where is this value used" on an unused value crash the page
  • Saved sort order that list views/reports follow: expected Entered / Alphabetical; list views, reports, dashboards follow it; actual Setting saved and field options follow it; list views and reports still sort A–Z (entered Silver, Platinum, Bronze → shown Bronze, Platinum, Silver). Zoho shows Silver, Platinum, Bronze
  • Countries and States list for address fields: expected List behind Country/State fields + Configure page; actual Not built: country/state fields still free text; only a "countries" predefined choice list
  • Used In lists reports, dependencies, blueprints: expected All places listed; actual Dependency maps + blueprints listed; reports not shown on screen (API field-usage finds them, body wrapped twice)

Zoho Desk comparison (live, 16 Nov): Zoho has no built-in Add comment action; a comment added through its comments API with the same HTML body (img onerror, b, javascript: link) is shown as safe rich text — onerror and the javascript: link stripped, broken image, bold, link without href, no script. TAVI now shows exactly the same. Decision (QA lead, 16 Nov 2026): accepted as matching Zoho, moved to Done. Hardening note for the developers: Zoho strips the dangerous attributes before saving; TAVI still stores the raw <img onerror> in the comment HTML and only cleans it on display, so email, API or export consumers could receive it raw.
